function.name: fs_read
function.description: Read a text file. Supports reading a window of lines instead of the whole file, which keeps large files out of the conversation.

path.description: File path relative to the workspace root.

offset.description: First line to read, 0-based. Defaults to 0.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read.

tail.description: Read only the last N lines. Overrides offset and limit.

function.name: fs_read_many
function.description: Read several text files in one call. Each file succeeds or fails independently.

offset.description: First line to read from each file, 0-based.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read from each file.

function.name: fs_list
function.description: List the direct contents of one directory. Use fs_tree for a recursive view and search_start to find files by name.

include_sizes.description: Include size and modification time for each entry.

function.name: fs_tree
function.description: Return a recursive directory tree up to a depth limit, ignoring dependency and build directories.

max_depth.description: Maximum depth to descend. Defaults to 3.

include_files.description: Include files as well as directories. Defaults to true.

function.name: fs_stat
function.description: Return basic metadata for a path: type, size, timestamps, mode, and whether it is a symlink. Use fs_info when content metrics or a hash are needed.

function.name: fs_info
function.description: Return the complete metadata of a file or directory: size, timestamps, permissions, ownership, inode details, and for text files the character, word and line counts, line ending style, encoding and a sha256 hash. Use fs_stat when only the basic type and size are needed.

include_hash.description: Compute a sha256 content hash. Defaults to true.

include_preview.description: Include the first and last lines of the file. Defaults to false.

preview_lines.description: How many lines to include in each preview. Defaults to 5.

max_depth.description: Depth limit when summarising a directory. Defaults to 10.

function.name: fs_roots
function.description: List the directories the filesystem tools are allowed to access.

function.name: fs_write
function.description: Create, overwrite, or append to a text file.

create_parents.description: Create missing parent directories. Defaults to true.

function.name: fs_edit
function.description: Replace an exact block of text in a file. Fails if the number of matches differs from expected_replacements, so an ambiguous edit is never applied silently.

old_text.description: Exact text to replace, including indentation.

expected_replacements.description: How many occurrences are expected. Defaults to 1.

function.name: apply_patch
function.description: Apply a strict unified diff to UTF-8 workspace files. Existing files can be edited; /dev/null headers can add files (parent directory must exist) or delete a whole file. All hunks and paths are validated before writes; one checkpoint covers the whole patch and a failed write rolls back.

paths.description: Workspace-relative paths, one for every file section in the patch.

patch.description: Unified diff with ---/+++ headers and @@ hunks; use /dev/null for file creation or whole-file deletion. Rename and partial-delete patches are unsupported; use fs_move or another filesystem tool.

function.name: checkpoint_undo
function.description: Restore files, directories, moves or deletes to the exact state captured by an earlier filesystem mutation. The undo itself creates a rollback checkpoint.

checkpoint_id.description: Checkpoint id returned by the earlier file mutation.

function.name: fs_mkdir
function.description: Create a directory, including missing parents.

function.name: fs_move
function.description: Move or rename a file or directory inside the workspace. Returns a checkpoint_id that can undo the move and restore an overwritten destination.

overwrite.description: Replace the destination if it already exists. Defaults to false.

function.name: fs_delete
function.description: Delete a file, symlink, or (with recursive=true) directory. Returns a checkpoint_id that can restore the deleted contents with checkpoint_undo.

recursive.description: Required to delete a non-empty directory.

function.name: search_start
function.description: Start a search over file contents or file names. Returns results directly when the search finishes within wait_ms, otherwise returns a search_id to poll.

query.description: Text, regular expression, or file name fragment depending on mode.

mode.description: Search file contents or file names. Defaults to content.

file_pattern.description: Only search files whose name matches this glob, such as *.js.

is_regex.description: Treat query as a regular expression.

case_sensitive.description: Match case exactly. Defaults to false.

max_results.description: Stop after this many matches. Defaults to 200.

wait_ms.description: How long to wait for completion before returning a handle. Defaults to 5000.

function.name: search_get
function.description: Fetch the results of a search started with search_start.

offset.description: Skip this many results, for paging through a large result set.

wait_ms.description: Wait up to this long for a still-running search to finish.

function.name: search_list
function.description: List searches known to the runtime and their status.

function.name: search_stop
function.description: Stop a running search and keep the results collected so far.

function.name: terminal_exec
function.description: Run a shell command to completion and return its exit code, stdout, and stderr. A non-zero exit code is returned as data, not as a tool failure. Use process_start for a command that does not finish on its own.

cwd.description: Working directory. Defaults to the workspace root.

timeout_ms.description: Kill the command after this many milliseconds. Defaults to 30000.

function.name: process_start
function.description: Start a background process or interactive PTY session that can be read from, written to, resized, and terminated. Use terminal_exec for commands that finish on their own.

cwd.description: Working directory. Defaults to the workspace root.

wait_ms.description: How long to collect initial output before returning. Defaults to 1000.

interactive.description: Start an interactive terminal session (PTY/ConPTY) instead of a piped process. The command is sent to the shell after startup.

cols.description: Initial PTY width in columns; defaults to 80.

rows.description: Initial PTY height in rows; defaults to 24.

function.name: process_read
function.description: Read output produced by a background process since the previous read.

wait_ms.description: Wait up to this long for new output to arrive.

peek.description: Return the full buffered output without advancing the read cursor.

function.name: process_write
function.description: Send input to the standard input of a running background process.

append_newline.description: Append a newline to the input. Defaults to true.

function.name: process_resize
function.description: Resize the terminal dimensions for an interactive PTY session.

cols.description: Terminal width in columns, from 20 to 400.

rows.description: Terminal height in rows, from 5 to 120.

function.name: process_terminate
function.description: Stop a background process with SIGTERM, escalating to SIGKILL if it does not exit.

grace_ms.description: How long to wait before escalating to SIGKILL. Defaults to 2000.

function.name: process_list
function.description: List background processes started by the runtime.

include_finished.description: Include processes that already exited. Defaults to false.

function.name: git_status
function.description: Show the current Git repository status: branch, staged, unstaged, and untracked files, in short format.

function.name: git_diff
function.description: Show changes in the Git working tree or the staging area.

staged.description: Show staged changes instead of working tree changes.

path.description: Limit the diff to this path.

context_lines.description: Number of context lines around each change.

function.name: git_log
function.description: Show recent Git commits as one line each, with decorations such as branch and tag names.

limit.description: Maximum number of commits. Defaults to 10.

function.name: git_branch
function.description: List local Git branches, or create a new one. Listing is read-only; creating changes the repository.

name.description: Branch name when creating a branch.

function.name: git_checkout
function.description: Switch the working tree to an existing Git branch. This changes the files on disk.

function.name: git_add
function.description: Stage specific paths for the next commit.

function.name: git_commit
function.description: Create a Git commit. When paths is supplied, commit only those paths and preserve unrelated staged changes.

paths.description: Optional path allowlist. Automatic hooks always provide this so unrelated staged files cannot enter the commit.

function.name: git_push
function.description: Push commits to a remote with the repository's own git credentials. Always needs approval. force is refused unless the operator enabled GIT_ALLOW_FORCE_PUSH, and is then sent as --force-with-lease. remote and branch are plain names, not refspecs.

remote.description: Remote name. Defaults to origin when branch is given; otherwise git's configured push target.

branch.description: Branch to push. Omit to push the current branch to its upstream.

set_upstream.description: Record the remote branch as the upstream (--set-upstream).

force.description: Overwrite the remote branch with --force-with-lease. Refused unless GIT_ALLOW_FORCE_PUSH is on.

function.name: git_worktree
function.description: Manage Git worktrees: list them, add one (only inside the workspace or a GIT_WORKTREE_ROOTS folder) on an existing ref or a new branch, or remove one of this repository's worktrees. add and remove need approval.

path.description: Worktree folder for add and remove, relative to cwd or absolute.

ref.description: Branch or commit to check out in a new worktree (add).

new_branch.description: Create this branch for the new worktree (add, git worktree add -b).

force.description: remove: also remove a worktree with uncommitted changes.

function.name: net_fetch
function.description: Fetch a URL over HTTP or HTTPS and return the response body as text. Loopback, link-local, cloud metadata, and private network addresses are refused.

timeout_ms.description: Abort the request after this many milliseconds. Defaults to 15000.

function.name: runtime_stats
function.description: Report what the runtime has actually executed: per-tool call counts, failures, timings, and the most recent tool calls.

include_recent.description: Include the recent call list. Defaults to true.

recent_limit.description: How many recent calls to include. Defaults to 10.

function.name: plan_get
function.description: Read the persistent real-work plan, assigned agents, next step, and the read-only runtime routine (before/after hooks).

summary_only.description: Return only the progress summary instead of every phase.

function.name: plan_set
function.description: Create or replace the real-work plan. Steps may name an agent profile. Runtime hooks are shown separately as routine and must not be copied into phases.

phases.description: Ordered phases. Each is an object with id, title, optional goal, and steps.

agent.description: Registered agent profile that owns this step, or null for the main agent.

evidence.description: Runtime evidence for the current status.

steps.description: Real work steps only. Each may assign an agent profile; runtime hooks do not belong in the plan.

preserve_progress.description: Keep the recorded status of steps that already exist. Defaults to true.

function.name: plan_update
function.description: Record progress: set the status of phases or steps, attach the evidence for a finished step, and add steps to a phase before starting it. A step cannot be marked done without evidence.

agent.description: Change or clear the agent profile assigned to this step.

add_steps.description: New steps for an existing phase.

agent.description: Registered agent profile that owns this step, or null for the main agent.

evidence.description: Runtime evidence for the current status.

id.description: Flat form: id of one phase or step to update.

evidence.description: Flat form: evidence for the update.

agent.description: Flat form: agent assignment for a step.

phase_id.description: Flat form: phase receiving new steps.

agent.description: Registered agent profile that owns this step, or null for the main agent.

evidence.description: Runtime evidence for the current status.

steps.description: Flat form: steps to add to phase_id.

function.name: memory_get
function.description: Read the working memory of this workspace: goals, decisions, requirements, constraints, facts, open tasks and finished work, plus how much history is kept in the archive behind it.

fields.description: Only these memory lists. Defaults to all of them.

include_archive.description: Include archive statistics. Defaults to true.

function.name: archive_search
function.description: Search the event archive of earlier work: every tool call folded out of the conversation is kept here with its title, its error and a preview. Use it to recover something the conversation no longer contains instead of redoing the work.

query.description: Keywords, such as a file name, an error text or a command.

agent.description: Only events produced by this agent.

tool.description: Only events produced by this tool.

min_importance.description: Drop records below this importance, between 0 and 1.

function.name: archive_get
function.description: Read the full stored body of archived events by id, as returned by archive_search.

function.name: skill_get
function.description: Load the full text of a skill: what it is for, how to do it, what to avoid, and which tools it uses. The prompt lists only skill names and descriptions, so read a skill before starting that kind of work.

function.name: skill_read
function.description: Read one resource of a skill that carries data, such as a house style, a checklist or a table. skill_get lists which resources a skill has.

resource.description: Resource id, as listed by skill_get.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read.

function.name: mcp_servers
function.description: List the configured MCP servers with their transport, connection state, tool count and any error. Use this first when an MCP tool is missing or failing.

refresh.description: Reconnect and re-read every server's tool list before answering.

function.name: mcp_tools
function.description: List the tools the connected MCP servers offer, with their parameter names. Each one can be called with mcp_call, or directly by its mcp__<server>__<tool> name when it is declared.

server.description: Only list the tools of this server.

refresh.description: Ask the servers again instead of using the cached catalogue.

limit.description: Maximum number of tools to return.

function.name: mcp_search_tools
function.description: Load the full definitions (description and input schema) of MCP tools that are not declared in this request. The runtime context lists them under mcp.deferred_tools by name and one line; search by words or exact names, then run one with mcp_call.

query.description: Words describing what the tool should do, or an exact tool name.

names.description: Exact tool names (mcp__<server>__<tool> or the server's own name) to load.

server.description: Only search the tools of this server.

limit.description: How many definitions to return (1-25, default 5).

refresh.description: Ask the servers again instead of using the cached catalogue.

function.name: mcp_call
function.description: Call a tool on an MCP server. Use this for any server tool, including one that is not declared as its own function. Name the server and the tool, or pass the full mcp__<server>__<tool> name as tool.

server.description: Server name, as reported by mcp_servers. Not needed when tool is a full mcp__<server>__<tool> name.

tool.description: Tool name on that server, or a full mcp__<server>__<tool> name.

arguments.description: Arguments for the tool, matching the schema mcp_tools reports.

timeout_ms.description: Override the call timeout for this one call.

function.name: mcp_add
function.description: Connect a new MCP server and make its tools available for the rest of the run. Give a command for a local stdio server, or a url for an http, sse or websocket one. The connection is proved before the server is kept.

name.description: Name to register the server under. Used as the prefix of its tool names.

transport.description: Transport to use. Inferred from command or url when omitted.

command.description: Executable or .js entry point for a stdio server.

url.description: Endpoint for an http, sse or websocket server.

env.description: Extra environment variables for a stdio server.

headers.description: Extra HTTP headers for a remote server.

token.description: Bearer token for a remote server.

include.description: Only expose these tools of the server.

exclude.description: Do not expose these tools of the server.

trust.description: How much approval calling this server needs. restricted always asks, trusted never does.

persist.description: Save the server to .agent/mcp.json so it is there next time. Defaults to true.

function.name: mcp_remove
function.description: Disconnect an MCP server and withdraw its tools for the rest of the run.

name.description: Name of the server to remove.

persist.description: Also remove it from .agent/mcp.json. Defaults to true.

function.name: mcp_resources
function.description: List an MCP server's resources and resource templates, or read one resource by its uri.

server.description: Server name, as reported by mcp_servers.

uri.description: Read this resource instead of listing them.

limit.description: Maximum number of resources to list.

function.name: mcp_prompts
function.description: List an MCP server's prompts, or render one prompt with its arguments into the messages it expands to.

server.description: Server name, as reported by mcp_servers.

name.description: Render this prompt instead of listing them.

function.name: mcp_build
function.description: Write a small dependency-free MCP server into the workspace (.agent/mcp-servers/<name>) from the node or python template, or from an OpenAPI JSON document, and load it at once: its tools are callable through mcp_call in this same conversation. After editing its tools file, call again with action reload.

action.description: create (default) writes and registers the server; reload restarts an existing one after its tools file was edited.

name.description: Server name: letters, digits, dot, dash or underscore.

tools.description: The tools, unless openapi is given.

body.description: Body of the handler: JavaScript for async handler(args) { … } or Python for def handler(args): …, returning the result.

openapi.description: A workspace path to an OpenAPI 3 JSON document, or the document itself; one tool per operation.

base_url.description: The API's base URL when the document has no absolute servers[0].url.

register.description: Start and load the server now (default true).

persist.description: Keep it for later runs (operator's user file, this project only). Default false: this process only.

overwrite.description: Replace a server of the same name already in the workspace.

function.name: discussion_start
function.description: Start a multi-agent discussion with selected specialist personas. Each persona reasons from different priorities (security vs speed, etc.). Observer decides when to finish and produces final synthesis.

task.description: The task description to discuss, e.g. 'Design user session storage for Next.js app with JWT'

personas.description: List of persona ids to include. Available: security, backend, database, frontend, architect, performance, qa, devops, cost, accessibility, data, compliance, mobile, ml, legacy
